learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands the operating principles of basic combinational and sequential digital circuits.
Possesses basic and ordered knowledge about serial communication standards (USART, I2C, SPI, 1-Wire).
Knows and understands the construction and operation of a microprocessor, microcomputer, and microcontroller.
Knows and understands the operating principles of basic peripheral devices found in microcontrollers.
Possesses general and systematized knowledge about programmable logic controllers (PLCs).
Knows and understands the principles of encoding numbers in the binary system and performing basic arithmetic operations in this system.
Knows and understands the basic principles of microcontroller programming.
Is able to write, load, and run a program that controls a selected microcontroller peripheral device.
Is able to convert numbers between decimal and binary systems and perform arithmetic operations.
Is able to minimize a logical function using Karnaugh maps and design a logic circuit that implements this function.
Is able to write, load, and run a simple program for a microcontroller.
Is familiar with the construction and possibilities of using programmable logic controllers (PLCs).
Is familiar with the most common serial communication standards (USART, I2C, SPI, 1-Wire).
Is familiar with the architectures of selected microcontrollers and their application possibilities.

syllabus_topics: Number systems. Number systems and their types (positional, non-positional, weighted, non-weighted, reflexive). Natural binary code. Hexadecimal code. Number conversion between systems. Number complement and negative number encoding. Basic arithmetic operations in the binary system on integers. Gray code. BCD code.

Basic digital circuits. Combinational and sequential circuits. Gates. Basic combinational circuits: decoders, multiplexers, demultiplexers, adders, comparators. Examples of integrated combinational circuits. Sequential circuits. Latches and flip-flops. Level and edge synchronization. Registers. Counters. Examples of integrated sequential circuits.

Microcomputer. Microprocessor, microcomputer and microcontroller. Microcomputer elements: microprocessor, buses (address and data), RAM memory (SRAM, DRAM), ROM memory (ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, Flash). Read and write cycle to/from memory. Architectures of microcomputer systems: von Neumann, Harvard and mixed. Characteristics of architectures.

Microprocessor. Microprocessor structure. Instruction execution cycle. Status word. Basic flags C, Z, V and N and auxiliary flags (S, H (AC)). Addressing modes. Stack. Microprocessor instruction list and the concept of assembler. Implementations of data transfer instructions, jumps (unconditional and conditional), subroutine calls and returns from subroutines, bit shifts and rotations.

Fundamentals of programming in assembly and C language. Elements of assembly source code: directive, instruction, instruction argument, label, comment. Allocating variables in memory. Examples of typical operations in assembly: 2- and 4-byte arithmetic, 2- and 4-byte number comparisons, encoding if-then and if-then-else branches, bitwise arithmetic (setting and clearing bit(s) in a register, testing bit(s) status) in assembly and C/C++ languages.

Microcontrollers. Microcontroller definition. Microcontroller parameters. Examples of 8-, 16-, 32-bit microcontroller families. Microcontroller structure using AVR ATxmega as an example. Memory map. Clock signal distribution. Basic peripherals. Overview of selected peripheral devices with handling examples: binary inputs/outputs (I/O), analog-to-digital converter (ADC), time-counter systems (TC).

Interrupts. Definition. Maskable and non-maskable interrupts. Interrupt vector. Interrupt controller. Order of interrupt handling. Priorities and the concept of interrupt preemption. Interrupt masking.
Examples of using peripheral devices and the interrupt system. Using a timer for periodic execution of the main program loop code. Matrix keyboard handling.

Serial communication interfaces. Division of communication interfaces: parallel/serial, synchronous/asynchronous, half/full duplex. Concept and elements of a data frame. Overview of available interfaces and their basic parameters. USART, RS232, RS422, RS485 interfaces, SPI interface, I2C interface, 1-Wire interface.

Programmable logic controllers (PLCs). Definition of a PLC controller. Controller structure and controller operation cycle. Types of PLC controllers (modular, compact, micro- and nanocontrollers) and examples. I/O packages - binary, analog, counter, specialized. Standard parameters of I/O signals. Communication modules. Fundamentals of PLC programming. Overview of programming languages defined in standard 61131-3.
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed by an examination. Laboratory classes are assessed based on the execution of laboratory classes and a report. Students are obliged to prepare for laboratory exercises, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Passing the module requires passing all laboratory classes.
